delta_text: Modern C++ codebases face a persistent tension between compile-time encapsulation and runtime flexibility, and the choice between header-only interfaces, named modules, and dynamic polymorphism shapes everything from incremental build times to final binary size.

Named modules promise faster compilation and stronger isolation by replacing the fragile textual inclusion model with an explicit import graph, but they require every translation unit to agree on module ownership and dependency direction,
which is why the Loom project enforces a directed acyclic graph at the responsibility-directory level and rejects cycles with a build-time graph check rather than relying on convention alone.

The result is a codebase where restructuring a directory is a one-line CMake change instead of a sweeping import rewrite, and where the compiler can reason about interface boundaries that were previously invisible to the build system.
